facts.content: Patient has swelling in the left elbow lasting one week.
The elbow is warm, fluid-filled, with mild tenderness adjacent to the tip and no pain on the tip.
facts.source_text: Warm, fluid-filled, mild tenderness adjacent to tip; no pain on tip; full ROM

facts.content: Patient has full range of motion in the elbow.
facts.source_text: Warm, fluid-filled, mild tenderness adjacent to tip; no pain on tip; full ROM

facts.content: There was no trauma and this is the first episode of elbow swelling.
Patient has a desk job and runs 2 to 3 times a week.
Patient has a history of osteoarthritis diagnosed by a general practitioner.
Patient is allergic to peanuts and denies drug allergies.
Video exam shows visible olecranon swelling with slightly dry, warmer skin than adjacent, mild focal tenderness, and full active range of motion.
facts.source_text: Video exam: visible olecranon swelling; overlying skin slightly dry, warmer than adjacent; mild focal tenderness; full active ROM

facts.content: Diagnosed with left olecranon bursitis, atraumatic.
Prescribed Ibuprofen 400 mg orally twice daily with food; advised to stop if dyspepsia occurs.
facts.source_text: Ibuprofen 400 mg PO BID with food; stop if dyspepsia

facts.content: Labs ordered include FBC, ESR/CRP, uric acid, and rheumatoid antibodies; form mailed to patient.
facts.source_text: Labs: FBC, ESR/CRP, uric acid, rheum antibodies; form mailed to pt

facts.content: Follow up by video or face-to-face after lab results in approximately one week.
Advised to seek urgent care if increased pain, redness, or spreading erythema occurs.
facts.source_text: Safety net: seek urgent care if ↑pain, redness, or spreading erythema
